summary: Okanogan Co., WA L-4 lookout cab built 1930 on Diamond Point at 7,916 ft; destroyed in 1952, with an outhouse seat and other debris still reported on site.

facts.design: 14-by-14-foot L-4 lookout cab; a Washington Lookouts page calls it an Aladdin lookout house
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1952 per the register and FireLookout.com. WillhiteWeb's photo captions show an outhouse seat, a double chair, and nails, glass and hinges at the site. No source describes a standing structure.

staffing.status: Howard Culp named as a lookout in an undated account; no staffing years given in the sources

access.note: Reached by a long hike from the Billy Goat Trailhead at the end of Eightmile Creek Road. No closure is mentioned in the sources. Fire has reduced the final mile to a faint path.

visit.trail_note: From Billy Goat Trailhead the route runs over Billy Goat Pass and Three Fools Pass, then a high pass burned in 2015, then cross-country up the ridge. Listed as 12 miles with 4,600+ feet of gain.

events.note: 14 by 14 foot L-4 lookout building, with materials packed over a 12-mile trail in December 1930. A Washington Lookouts page calls it an Aladdin lookout house.
Washington Lookouts quotes a July 1931 Wenatchee Daily World item: three new lookouts went out, and R.G. Dykstra of Omak went to Diamond Peak. The page does not say whether this site is meant.
Panorama photos taken September 17, 1934; the register credits them to the National Archives Pacific Northwest Region.
Howard Culp is named as a lookout in an account from a lookout book, quoted by WillhiteWeb. No year is given.
Cab destroyed in 1952 per the register, FireLookout.com and WillhiteWeb. The sources do not give a cause.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register, FireLookout.com and WillhiteWeb call the building an L-4 cab or L-4 lookout building. Washington Lookouts calls it an Aladdin lookout house. The story uses L-4 and reports the other name.
The 1931 item quoted by Washington Lookouts names its destination Diamond Peak, not Diamond Point. The story does not treat that item as a record of this site's staffing.

sources.title: Diamond Point Lookout Site - Pasayten Wilderness

notes_for_editor: Brief kind 'ground' is not stated in any source; the sources describe only a cab, so the record may be right but is unverified. The 1930 and 1952 dates appear on all four pages, but the register and FireLookout.com share wording, so they are not independent. The Culp anecdote is undated. The 1931 Dykstra item may mean this site under another name; it is coded as other, not staffing. The 1946 caption event is the page's photo caption, not a separate record. No photos added; WillhiteWeb photos have no image URLs.
